subject: general
question: With which dance form is the noted dancer Guru Rajkumar Singhajit Singh associated?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Manipuri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Manipuri Dance**
 
• The Manipuri Dance also referred to as the Manipuri Raas Leela, is one of the eight major Indian classical dance forms, originating in the state of Manipur__.
 __
 
• Manipuri is one of the six classical dance forms of India, the others being Bharata Natyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi and Odissi.
 
• It is indigenous to Manipur and is characterized by a variety of forms that are associated with folk tradition and ritual.
 
• Varieties of Manipuri Dance Styles:
 
 
• Raas
 
• Nata-Sankirtan
 
• Pung Cholam (Dancers play the pung/drum while dancing)
 
• Dhola Cholam
 
• Kartal Cholam
 
• Thang ta (martial art form)
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kathak:

 
 
• ​Kathak is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance.
 
• It is the classical dance form of Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The origin of Kathak is traditionally attributed to the travelling bards in ancient northern India known as Kathakars or storytellers.
 
 

 
• **Odissi**
 
• Odissi is one of the classical dance forms of India which originated in the state of Odisha.
 
 
• It is known for its unique style and grace, characterized by its fluid movements and intricate gestures.
 
• The dance form is deeply rooted in the culture and traditions of Odisha and is often performed in temples as a form of worship.
 
• Odissi dance has a rich history and has been mentioned in ancient texts such as the Natyashastra.
 
• The dance form is traditionally performed by women, but in modern times, it has also been performed by men.
 
 
 
• **Kathakali**
 
 
• Kathakali is a classical dance form that originates from Kerala, a state in the southern part of India.
 
• It is distinguished by its vibrant costumes, elaborate makeup, and face masks that the performers wear.
 
• Kathakali translates to "Story-Play" and is known for its intricate storytelling, detailed gestures, and expressive eye movements.
 
• The dance form combines dance, music, drama, and literature into a composite art form, making it unique and complex.
 
• Themes of Kathakali are mostly taken from the Indian epics like Mahabharata, Ramayana, and other ancient scriptures.
 
• It is performed exclusively by men and involves rigorous physical training to master the art form.
 
• The music used in Kathakali is called Sopanam and is sung in the Malayalam language.
